title: THE DELEGATION FILES
credit: Based on “Your coding agents made you a manager” by Addy Osmani

lines.text: Three oh seven A.M. The agent has been running for nine hours.
lines.caption: 3:07 AM. The agent has been running for nine hours.

lines.name: THE NIGHT SHIFT
lines.text: Why babysit it? Start it before bed. Check it in the morning.
Nobody told it what done looked like. By sunrise, four thousand lines, built on a wrong premise.
If you work with coding agents, you're already a manager. These are the habits that betray you.

scenes.verdict: Give it a way to check its work.

lines.text: It looks done. Ship it.
Looks done isn't done. Give it a test, a build, a screenshot. Then ask for the proof.

scenes.verdict: Tell it what it can't see.

lines.text: Make the dashboard faster. It'll figure it out.
Skip what the code already says. Give it the goal, the why, the limits, and what done means.
I'll just fix it again. Every session.
Corrected it twice? Write it into Claude dot M D, or make it a skill.

scenes.verdict: Let it decide. Enforce only what can't bend.

lines.text: Never! Always! Think harder!
Over-process is the new micromanagement. Hard rules only for what must never bend.

evidence: slice A │ slice B │ slice C

lines.text: Five agents, same task. Five times the output!
No. One merge conflict with five authors. Plan first, and split the work so nothing overlaps.
One more correction. This time it'll work.
Two failed fixes means the problem is upstream. Start fresh, with a better prompt.

scenes.verdict: Delegate the task, never the judgment.

lines.text: Six hundred lines. Tests are green. Approve.
That isn't review. That's ratification. Treat every diff like you'll get paged for it.

scenes.verdict: Design the run that doesn't need you.

lines.text: It'll stop when it's finished.
Before any unattended run, answer five questions. Done, checks, boundaries, limits, and who signs off.
Forty percent of our code is written by AI!
That's activity, not quality. Count the reverts. Add agents only as fast as your checks can watch them.

evidence: How will we know it worked?

lines.text: It's cheap. Build everything.
Building is cheap. Reviewing isn't. The question isn't can we. It's should we.

evidence: eager to agree, quick to overtrust

lines.text: I run five agents. So I can manage five people.
You can't. People are harder. Agents are eager, confident, and all the same.

evidence: ask it to argue against itself

lines.text: Just trust the machine.
Make it argue against its own answer. And own every line that ships.
You don't need the title. Be the reason good code gets written.
